۱ ٥٥ 
Whether the termination of service of Shri Balai Chandra 
Debnath in justified ? To what relief, if any, is 
he entitled 1 

On receipt of the order of reference, usual notices were 
served on the parties and they appeared and filed: written 
statements. Thereafter 7th March 1967 was fixed for 
hearing of the case. On that date the Company was 
preseht but neither the cdhcerned worker nor anybody 
on behalf of the Union appeared. By order passed 
on that date the Union was directed to explain by 
13th March 1967 its absence on that date. No explana- 
tion, however, was submitted by the Union on 13th 
March 1967 and instead Shri Jagannath Pandey, Presi- 
dent of Road Transport Mazdoor Congress, filed a peti- 
tion for adjournment of the hearing of the case. On that 
petition the case was adjourned to 20th March 1967 for 
hearing. On 20th March 1967 Company appeared but 
again. the Union and the concerned worker were absent. 
From this repeated non-appearance of the Union and 
the concerned workman on dates fixed for hearing of 
the case, it is presumed that none is eager to pursue the 
matter. Accordingly a “no dispute’’ award on the 
footing that the industrial dispute under reference is no 
longer in existence is passed.

NOTIFICATION 


IN accordunce with the provisions of sub-section (4) of 
section 126 of the Calcutta Port Act, 1890 (Bengal Act 
111 of 1880), the following new by-law No. 14-A which the 
Commissioners propose to incorporate in the by-laws for 
the Port of Calcutta is hereby published for genoral 
information : 


By-law No. 14A 


“In the absence of firm programme for a vessel occupy- 
ing a berth, mooring and/or buoy, she may be 
ordered to sail to Sandheads. The vessel con- 
cerned shall carry out such an order without any 
unreasonable delay.” 


2’. The ৮ by-law will be submitted to the Gov- 
ernment of India for confirmation on the expiry of fourteen 
days after tho first publication of this Notification in -the 
State Gazette and commenta or criticisms, if any, with 


regurd thereto received by the undersigned within ‘that 
period will be considered. 


T. R. RAGHUPATHL 
Secretary.

Notice is hereby given that— 


(1) an election is to be held of seven members by the members of the 
West Bengal Legislative Assembly; 


(2) forms of nomination paper may be obtained at the office of the 
Returning Officer at Assembly House, Calcutta, between the hours 
of 11 in the morning and 5 in the afternoon from the 20th April, 
1967 to the 27th April, 1967; 


(3) nomination papers may be delivered between the hours of 11 in the 
morning and 5 in the afternoon by a candidate or his proposcr 
or seconder to the Returning Officer at his office on any day not 
later than the 27th April, 1967; 


(4) the nomination papers will be taken up for scrutiny at 11-00 a.m. 
on the 29th April, 1967, at the Assembly House, Calcutta; 


(5) notice of withdrawal of candidature may be delivered by a candidate, 
or his authorised election agent to the Returning Officer at his 
Office before 5 p.m. on the 2nd May, 1967; 

(6) in the event of the election being contested, a poll shall be taken, 
by means of Postal Ballot Papers. The poll shall be closed at 
3 p.m. on the 24th May, 1967. 


P. ROY, 


Returning Officer and Secretary, West Bengal 
Legislative Assembly, 


Date—The 20th April, 1967. 
Place—Assembly House, Calcutta.

PART L—Orders and notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government 
Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 


ORDER 


No. 2809-F.S/FS /14R-87 /67.—26th April 1967.—Whereas the Governor 
is of opinion that it 1s necessary and expedient so to do for maintaining 
supplies of rice and paddy in West Bengal; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 of the 
Kasential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955), read with the Government 
of India, Ministry of Food, Agriculture, Community Development and Co- 
operation (Department of Food) Order No. G.S.R. 906, dated the 9th June 
1966, as subsequently amended, the Governor is pleased hereby to make, 
with fie prior concurrence of the Central Government, the following Order, 
namely :— 


1. Short titic, extent and commencement.—(1) This Order may be 
es the West Bengal Rice and Paddy (Notification of Movement) Order, 
1967. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal, except the areas in which 
the West Bengal Rationing Order, 1964, is in force. 


(3) It shall come into force at once. 


2. Dofinitions.—In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires,--- 


(a) 00100011975 means, in respect of any area constituted as a 
municipality under any law for the time being in force, the 
Subdivisional Controller of Food and Supplies 11) the Depart- 
ment of Food and Supplies, Government of West Bengal having 
jurisdiction in such area, and in respect of any other area the 
Bleck Development Officer, having jurisdiction im such 
area and includes such other officer of the State Government as 
may be authorized by the State Government by. notification in 
the “Official Gazette’? to perform the functions of the 
Controller under this Order in respect of such areas aa may be 
specified in the notification; 


132] 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, APRIL 26, 1967 [Part I‏ 9اا 
I a ere‏ 


(9) ‘‘declarant’’ means a person who makes a declaration under the 
provisions of this Order; 


(c) ‘‘declaration’’ means a declaration in the form specified in the 
Schedule to this Order; 


(0) ‘‘place of deapatch’’ and ‘‘place of destination’? mean respectively 
the places where transport commences or is intended to commence 
and where transport terminates or is intended to terminate; 


(e) ce includes broken rice, but does not include chira, muri or 
101; 


(1) ‘‘free limit’? means a quantity not exceeding 9} quintals, whether 
in puldy, or in paddy equivalent of rice or in both taken together, 
as the case may be; 


Explanation.—For the purpose of this clause, the expression 
‘paddy equivalent of rice’? means in respect of a quantity of 
rice a quantity of paddy equal to one end a half times the 
quantity of rice. 


(g) ‘‘transport’’ means to move or cause to be moved by any means 
whatsoever. 


3. Submission of declaration to Controller before commencement and 
after completion of transport.—(1) No person shall transport any rice or 
paddy exceeding the free limit from any place to any other place, until he 
has submitted a declaration in triplicate to the Controller having jurisdic- 
tion in the place of despatch and until he has received back from such 
Controller two copies of the declaration endorsed by such Controller with 
his signature and seal together with the serial number and date of such 
endorsement. 


(2) The Controlller, to whom a declaration is submitted under sub- 
paragraph (1), shall make an endorsement thereon in the manner indicated 
in the said sub-paragraph and shall thereafter return the endorsed copies 
of the declaration to the declarant and retain the third copy thereof. 


(3) Every declarant shall transport rice or paddy in conformity with 
his declaration after it has been endorsed under sub-paragraph (1) and shall, 
after transporting rice or paddy to the place of destination, but before 
selling or otherwise disposing of the stock or any, portion thereof, specify 
the quantity or quantities of rice or paddy or both actually transported in 
the endorsed copies of the declaration and submit them to the Controller 
having jurisdiction in the place of destination. 


(4) The Controller, to whom the endorsed copies of the declaration are 
submitted under sub-paragraph (3), shall forthwith mark them with the 
word ‘‘secen’’ under his signature with date and his seal 050 ehall 
thereafter return one of the copies to the declarant and retain the other. 


4. Savings.—Nothing in this Order shall apply to transport of any rice 
or paddy— 
(i) on account of or on behalf of the State Government or the Central 
Government or the Food Corporation of India established under . 


the Food Corporations Act, 1964 (37 of 1964); 


(ii) covered by a permit or an order of exemption issued under the 
West Bengal Essential Food stuffs Anti-Hoarding Order, 1966, 
or under the West Bengal Rice Mills Control] Order, 1967, or by 
a permit issued under the West Bengal Rice (Movement 
Control) Order, 1964; 


(iii) under and in accordance with military credit notes. 


5. Powers of entry, search, seizure, etc.—(1) The Controller or any 
officer of the Department of Food and Supplies, not below the rank of Sub- 
Inspector or any Police Officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub- 
Inspector or such other gazetted officer of the State Government as may be 
authorised by the State Government in this behalf, may, with a view to 
securing compliance with this Order, or to satisfying himself that this 
Order has been complied with, with such aid or assistance, as he thinks 

{,— 
(a) stop and search any person or any vessel found in inland water- 
wavs, or any vehicle or animal or receptacle used or capable of 
being used for the transport of rice or paddy;

(৮) inspect any document relating to transport, sale or disposal of rice 
or paddy; 
(c) enter and search any premises or place; 


(d) seize and remove any article in respect of which he suspects that 
any provision of this Order has been, is being or is about to be 
contravened, along with the packages, coverings or receptacles 
in which such article is found and the animals or vehicles or 
vessels or other conveyances used in carrying such article and 
thereafter take or authorise the taking of all measures necessary 
for securing the production of the article, packages, coverings, 
receptacles, animals, vehicles, vessels or other conveyances ৪0 
seized, in a court and for their safe custody pending such 
production. 


(2) The provisions of sections 102 and 103 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898), relating to search and seizure, shall, so far 
us may be, apply to searches and seizures under this paragraph.

: The 20th March 1967.

6201)01) of the Calcutta Police Act, 1866 (Act IV of 
1866), and under section 39(1)(j) of the Calcutta

do hereby prohibit hookswinging and other modes of 
self-torture on the occasion of “Charak Puja” for the 
maintenance of public safety and prevention of dis- 
turbance at a place of public assembly within any 

rt of the town and suburbs of Calcutta as defined 
ا‎ the Calcutta Police Act, 1866 (Act IV of 1866), 
and notified under the Calcutta Suburban Police Act, 
1866 (Act II of 1866),

of the Dentists Act. 1948 (Act XVI of 1948), under 
clause (b) of sub-section (1) of the seetion 22 of 
the said Act for the period of five years; 


Aud whereas the term of the said agreement 
expired on the Twelfth Day of September 1966 and 
the Government of Tripurn haa requested the 
(dovernor of the Stute of West Bengal (Appendix I) 
for renewal of the said agreement for a further 
period of five years; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power con- 
ferred under sub-section (1) of section 22 of the 
Dentists Act, 1948 (Act XVI of 1948), the Governor 
was pleased to extend the terme of the said Agrov- 
ment for a further period of five years with effect 
from the 13th September 1966.

published at paze 868, Part Il, section 3 of the

and Microwave Station in the village of Darjeeling,

with the said notification, to whom it may concern.

Order, 1966, of Government of India, Ministry of 
Food and Agriculture, Community Development and 
Corporation (Department of Food) (published under 
their Order No. GSR-912 ESS.Com/Sugar, dated 
10th June 1966) to me under the Government of 
West Bengal, Department of Food and Supplies, 
Notification No. 6133/FS, dated 215 June 1966, 
read with Order No. 3457/FS, dated 27th May 1966, 
of the Department of Food and Supplies, Govern- 
ment of West Bengal, and in accordance with the 
instructions issued by the Central Government in 
this behalf, I, the District Magistrate of Nadia, 
hereby fix the transport costs and other incidental 
charges and also selling rates in respect of sale of 
undermentioned grade of sugar, chargeable by the 
different categories of dealers in areas of this district 
as shown in the schedule below— 


Schedule 


(A) Name of sugar mill of importer from whom 
sugar was imported—The Deoria Sugar 
Mills Ltd., Deoria. 


(B) Grade of sugar—D-29. 


(C) Ex-Factory/importer price of sugar per 
quintal—Rs. 139.10 P. 


Area in which the order will be operative— 
Santipur. 


Transport costs including Railway freight and 
incidental charges chargeable by the whole- 
saler per quintal—Rs. 8.35 P. 


Maximum prefit allowable to the wholesaler per 
quintal—Rs. 2. 68. P. 


Maximum wholesale selling rate chargeable by 
the wholesaler per quintal—Rs. 150.13 P. 


Maximum profit, incidental charges allowable to 
retailer per quintal—Rs. 2.87 P. 


Maximum retail selling rate per kilogram charge- 
able by the retailer—Rs. 1.53 P. 


Explanation.—In this order— 


(1) “Dealer” means any person carrying on the 
business of purchasing ‘selling and includes 
wholesalers and retailers. 


(2) “Retailer” means any person who sells sugar 
to a consumer not being a dealer. 


(3) “Wholesaler” means a dealer who sells to 
any other dealer and including a broker, 
commission agent or any other agent having 
authority to sell sugar belonging to his 
principal. 


(4) Retail price fixed above is applicable within 
8 kilometer from the wholesalers’ godown. 
It shall increase by one paisa per kilogram 
for every slab of 8 kilometer beyond first 
8 kilometer.

In the matter of an industrial dispute between Messrs.

being a question of law might be decided on some ad- 
mitted facta. Facts admittcd by both the sides are 
as follows : 


The company has its factory and Head Office at 
Goabaria, Howrah. The Sales Division of the 
company is at Camac Street, Calcutia. The 
company has got several branch cfficer in 
diffcrent Stutes outside West Bengal. The Balance 
Shect and Profit and Loss Accounts are prepared 
on the basis of the assets, liabilities, prufits and 
losses of the company in respuct of the 
factorics, Hcad Office, 99109 Division and different 
branches taken together. It is also admitted 
that it is not possible to ascertain profit and loss 
of any of tho factory, Head Office, Sales Division 
or branches taken seperately. Some Balance 
Sheets and Profit and Loss Accounts have been 
filed in this case. There is no dispute that in 
the factory of the company there are two unions, 
namely, thefEmployees’ Union and the Worker's 
Union. There is no dcubt also that there is one 
Head Office Employees’ Union for the workmen 
of the Head Office. It is also ৪, fact that at the 
instance of the Employees’ Union several disputes 
between the company and its factory workmen 
were raised, and some references were sent to the 
Tribunal and decided. Similarly at the instance 
of the Head Office Employees’ Union some dis- 
putes were raised and decided by the Industrial 
Tribunal in respect of the workmen of the Head 
Office. There is no dispute before moe also that 
none of the unions of the factory workmen es- 
poused the cause of the workmen of the لئ‎ 
Office or the branch offices. Similarly, The 
Head Office Employees’ Union never took up 
the cause of the workmen of the companys’ 
factory. It فا‎ also admitted before me at the 
time of argument that the Head Office 
Employees’ Union has started a proceeding 
before the Government Conciliation Officer on 
the same question of bonus as involved in the 
present proceeding and that the said matter 
is still under consideration of the Government.

The Standing Orders of the company will appear 
in Ext. E. Section 13 of the Standing Orders relates to 
disciplinary action for misconduct. According to this 
section there are certain acts and ommissions mentioned 
in clause (c) ‘as misconduct. Section 13(c) (viii) speaks 
about riotous or disorderly behaviour on the Estate 
prejudicial to the good running of the Estate or any 
act subversive of discipline. For an offence under 
section13(c) (viii) an oumployee may be dismissed at any 
time but for a first offence under section 13(c)(xii) 
no worker shall be dismissed. In the present case. 
however, all the charge-shected persons were alleged 
to have 1১060 committed misconduct under section 
13(c) (viii) of the Standing Orders. In the present 
case I have considered the statements of the witnesses 
of both the sides and also the documentary evidence 
and I am satisfied that the delinquents were duly 
charge-sheeted, that they were given opportunity to 
submit their explanation in reply to the charge-sheet, 
that at the enquiry charges were explained to 679 
delinquents who were given opportunity to be represent- 
ed at the enquiry, that the company’s witnesses were 
at first examined and then offered for cross-examination 
by the delinquents and that the delinquents were 
also given sufficient opportunity to make statement and 
to examine defence witnesses. I am also satisfied that 
the records of the proceedings were faithfully prepared 
at the enquiry. After the conclusion of the enquiry,

according te the Standing Orders, the delinquents were 
given notice under section 13(g) offering an opportunity 
for making representation through union official before 
the passing of the order of dismissal or suspension as 
punishment. In fact, representation by the union 
was made bofore the Managor who gave patient hearing. 
1 have marked the demeanow of the witnesses on the 
side of the union and also by the way in which they gave 
evidence. They made statements like parrots and 
their evidence I cannot accept as true. O.P.Ws. 
ا‎ and 2 gave straightforward evidence and | ৮০115 
believe that the records of procecdings appearing in 
Exts. U and 0/1 are genuine. I am also satistied 
that the enquiries were held as stated by O.P.Ws. 
1 and 2 according to the principles of natural justice 
and the Standing Orders of the company. There had 
been no occasion at the enquiry to cause any prejudice 
to the charge-sheeted persons who got proper oppor- 
tunity for their self-defence. I have also considered 
the findings arrived at by the enquiring officers. In 
the findings reasons are given. Tho findings are not 
without any hasis. They are reasonable hased = on 
legal evidence collected at the enquiry. I do not find 
any basic error of fact there. 


It has been argued from theside ofthe union that 
no sufficient time was given to the delinquents aftor 
the charge-sheot for giving evidence at the enquiry. 
Tt has been submitted that after the submission of 
the explanations in reply of the charge-sheet the delin- 
quents should have been given sometime. The evidence 
shows that the delinquents got sufficient time to pre- 
pare themselves for the enquiry. Moreover, none of the 
oharge-shveted persons prayed for time for getting ready 
or for adjournment of the hearing at the enquiry. 
All opportunitiés were given to the delinquents for 
proper representation of their cases with the help of 
their co-workers. The management Made arrangement 
for bringing the witnesses and the representatives 
on the side of the charge-shceted persons if so desired. 
There had been no occasion to projudice the 0856 of the 
delinquents. 


It has been contended from the side of the workmen 
that according to the section 13(e) of the Standing Orders 
the Manager should have recorded his reasons if he 
finds the explanation unacceptable. In this case this 
provision has been, complied with. The records of the 
proceedings will show that the explanations submitted 
by the delinquents were recorded and that the findings 
will show that the explanations were not accepted by 
the Manager. In the present case there has been 
sonie delay in taking disciplinary action against the 
delinquents and from the evidence of O.P.W.1 it will 
appear that he gave reasons for delay in giving the 
order of punishment. O.P.W.3 Alexander Elliot, the 
Manager who issued charge-shects has stated that had 
he issued the charge-sheets on the day of incident the 
workmen would have beon more vivlent as the situation 
was 80 tenso. This was the reason why there was somo 
dolay in issuing the charge-sheet. Moreover, delay 
was further due to the fact that charge-sheets had to be 
cyolostyled. In this case thorefore the delay was 
reasonable. The facts and circumstances do not show 
that the conduct of the company was motivated or that 
there was any want of good faith.

General intormation relating to age concession, fixation of 
initeal pay, eto., in respect of posts advertised by the 
Commission and instructions to candidates applying in 
response thereto. 


General concession in age 


(1) (a) For political sufferers: A candidate who before 
16th August 1947 was detained, imprisoned, interned or 
externed on account of his/her activities in connection with 
the country’s struggle for independence, not being convict- 
ed of an offence Saati a moral turpitude, shall be entitled 
to a concession in respect of the upper age limit. 
voncession granted wil] be equal to the exact period of 
detention, imprisonment, internment or externment suffered 
ap to a maximum of four yonrs. 


(b) For Soheduled Caste/Tribe candidates; The upper 
age limit is relaxable by five years for candidates belonging 
to Scheduled Castes /Scheduled Tribes. 


(9) For Displaced Persons: The upper age limit is 
relaxable up to 46 yeurs for displaced persone who have 
migrated to India from East Pakistan on or after January 


1, 1964. This concession in age aha) remain in force up to 
December 31, 1967. 


The bona fide of the displuced persons will have to be 
certified by the Camp Commandant of the Transit Centre 
of the Dandakaranya Project or the Camp Commandant of 
the Relief Camp in various States or the District Magis- 
trate of the arca where the candidate may for the time 
being be reside *. 


Fixation of Pay 


(2) (م)‎ For persons already in permanent Government 
service: If a permanent Government servant is permitted 
to apply and is selected for a post in open competition with 
outsiders, the initia] pay will be fixed under rule 42 or 55 
of the West Bengal Service Rules, Part I, as the case may 
be. If, however, such a recruit is pre _to resign his 
appointment under Government, before applying, he will be 
eligible to the grant of higher initial pay on the same basis 
as an outsider. 


(b) For a temporary Government servant having ne lien 
on any post under the West Bengal Government when 
appointed to a post oarrying higher soale of pay: Such 
an officer shall be eligible to draw as initial pay at the 
atage of the time-scale in the higher post which is equal 
to his pay in the lower post, or if there is no such stage, 
the stage next below that pay plus persomal pay equal to 
the difference, to be absorbed in future increments in the 
higher scale provided that he has already rendered at least 
three years’ continuous and satisfactory servicer in the 
lower post. The aforesaid benefit of fixation of pay will 
not, however, be available in the following cases: 


(1) when the Commission has made ৪ specific recom: 
mendation regarding the pay to be wed to the 


Officer; 


(ii) when under any specific rule auch an officer is 
allowed a higher initial pay. 

(c) For Outsiders: Unless otherwise specified in s 
particular advertisement, higher initial on the basis of 
age, qualifications and experience (including experience out- 
aide Government service) may allowed to a person not 
already in Government service, if the relevant advertise- 
ment contains a provision to that effect.

PART L—Orders and Notifications by the Governor of West Bengal, the High Court, Government

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND SUPPLIES 


ORDER 


No. 2861-F.S. /FS/14R-88/67.—27th April 1967.—Whereas the Gover- 
nor is of opinion that it is necessary and expedient so to do for maintaining 
supplies of rice and paddy and for securing their equitable distribution and 
availability at fair prices in West Bengal; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by section 3 of the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955), and in particular, sub- 
section (3B) thereof, read with the Government of India, Ministry of Food, 
Agriculture, Community Development and Co-operation (Department of 
Food), Order No. G.S.KR. 906, dated the 9th June 1966, as subsequently 
amended, the Governor is pleased hereby to make, with the prior 
concurrence of the Central Government, the following order, namely :— 


1. Short title, extent and comméncement.—(1) This Order may be 
called the West Bengal Foodgraing (Procurement) Order, 1967. 


(2) It extends to the whole of West Bengal except the areas in which 
the West Bengal Rationing Order, 1964, is for the time being in force. 


(3) It shall come into force at once. 


2. (Definitions.—In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) ‘‘family’’ includes servants living in the same mess; 

(b) ‘Food Corporation’? means the Food Corporation of India, 
established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 (37 of 1964), 
acting through its officers and agents as an agent of the Govern- 
ment for the purposes of this Order; 

(০) ‘‘foodgrains’’ meuns paddy or rice; 

(d) ‘‘Government’’ means the Government of the State of Wess 
Bengal; ° |

(e) ‘holding’, in relation to a producer, means the land or lande held 
by the producer, being not less than 10 acres in an_ irrigated 
area or 12 acres in a non-irrigated area or a total of 12 acres, :f 
partly in an irrigated area and partly in a non-irrigated area, 
on which or part of which foodgrains are grown or from which 
or part of which foodgrains are receivable by the producer; 
(f) ‘‘irrigated 87981” means an area within the command of any of the

(i) Damodar Valley Project, 
(ii) Mayurakshi Reservoir Project, 
(211) Kangsubati Reservoir Project, 
(iv) Power-driven Deep Tubewell Irrigation Projects, and 
(v) such other projects or plans as may be determined by the 
District Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner of a district in 
consultation with the Executive Engineer concerned of the 
Irrigation and Waterways Department of the Government to 
be irrigation projects for the purpose of this Order; 
(g) ‘‘non-irrigated area’? means an area other than an irrigated area; 


(h) ‘‘procurement agent’? meaus a person who has entered into an 
agreement with the Government for purchase, sale or storage wf 
foodgrains on bebalf of the Government and includes the Food 
Corporation ; 

(i) ‘procurement price’’ ineans, in relation to any variety and grade 
uf paddy or rice, the price specified in this Order for such variety

post-harvest period in respect of such variety and grade of paddy 
or rice; 

(j) ‘‘producer’’? means a person, who, as raiyat, under-raiyat, lessee, 
trustee, mortgagee in possession, sebait, mutwalli or bargadar 
or in any other capacity or in more than one such capacity, 
grows foodgrains or receives or is entitled to receive foodgrains, 
or & portion or a share thereof, grown on any holding or part 
thereof, whether such holding is cultivated by such person himself 
or by any other person; 

(k) ‘requirement of foodgrains’’, in relation to a producer, means the 
requirement of foodgrains of a producer for all or any of the

ap 8 procurement price by, the procurement agent to whom they are

and shall keep two carbon copies of each such receipt with an acknowledge- 
ment thereon by the producer of his having received the full price.

6. Appeals.—(1) Any producer, aggrieved by a notice served by the 
requiring اس‎ under sub-paragraph (3) of paragraph 3, or by any 
direction contained therein, may, within 30 days from the date of receipt 
by him of such notice, prefer an appeal to such magistrate of the first class 
having jurisdiction in the area as may be appointed by the District 
Magistrate or Deputy Commissioner of the district to be an appellate officer 
under this Order by a notification in the Official Gazette. 


(2) On receiving anu appeal the appellate officer appointed under sub- 
paragraph (1) shall after giving the appellant an opportunity of being 
heard and after taking such evidence as ie deems necessary dispose of the 
appeal as expeditiously us possible. 


7. Power of entry, search, seizure, ett.—(1) Any officer of the Depart- 
ment of Food and Supplies not below the rank of Sub-Iuspector or any 
Police Officer not below the rank of Assistant Sub-Inspector may, with 0 
view to securing compliance with this Order or to satisfying himself that 
this Order has been complied with,— 


(a) imspect or cause to be inspected any book or document or accounts 
as well as any stock of foodgrains belonging to or under the 
control of a producer, 


(b) require any person to give any information in his possession with 
respect to any foodgrains, ~~ 

(c) stop and search forthwith with such aid or assistance as may he 
necessary aby person or vehicle or vessel or anima] used or 
suspected of being used for delivery of foodgrains from eny 
টন where he has reason to believe that foodgrains ure 
stored, 


(0) enter and search with such aid or assistance as may be necessary 
any such premises, 


(e) seize and remove with such aid or assistance as may be necessary. 


any stock of foodgrains along with the packages, coverings or 
receptacles in which such stock is found and the animals, 
vehicles or vessels used in carrying such stock, 1£ he has reason 
to suspect that any provision of this Order has been, is being or 
is about to be, contravened in respect of such stock or any part 
thereof or in respect of any other stock of foodgrains which, 
immediately before the contravention, was stored along with 
such stock and thereafter take or authorise the taking of all 
measures necessary for securing the production of the stocks of 
foodgrains, packages, coverings, receptacles, animals, vehicles 
or vessels, so seized, in a court of law and for their safe custody 
pending such production. 


The provisions of sections 102 and 103 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898), relating to search and seizure shall, so far 
us may be, apply to searches and seizures under this paragraph. 


8. Powers to exempt in special cases.—IJf the Government, having 
regard to the conditions prevailing in any area, considers if necessary or

Official Gazette, exempt subject to such conditions as it may think fit to 
impose, such class or classes of producers in that area as it may specify in 
و‎ notification, from the operation of all or any of the provisions of this

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, 
CALCUTTA 


ORDER 


Whereas there is apprehension of assembly of 
five or more persons or procession or the doing of 
any act likely to cause disturbance of ublic 
tranquillity in the area mentioned in the schedule 
below (hereinafter referred to as the said area) ; 


And whereas, I, P. K. Sen, Commissioner of 
Police, Calcutta, being a Presidency Magistrate, 
have been specially empowered by the State 
Government under notification No. 180-G.A., dated 
the 14th January 1964, to act under section 144 of 
£১১8১০৫০ of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Aot 5 of 


And whereas, in my opinion, there is sufficient 
ground for proceeding under the said section for 
prohibition of assembly of five or more persons or 
any procession or the doing of any act likely to 
cause disturbance of the public tranquillity within 
the said area; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 144 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act 5 of 1898), read with 
sub-section (3) of the said section, I, the said 
P. K. Sen, Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, do 
hereby prohibit from the 2nd May 1967, until 
further orders, any agsembly of five or more persons 
or anv procession or the doing of any act which is 
likely to cause a disturbance of the public tran- 
quillity within the said area.

uppears that some dealers having Baby Food licences 
could not apply for their renewal in time gpd/or could 
not have the licences renewed after expiry গাঁ the period 
of their validity by 31st December 1966 for some 
reason or other; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred 
on me by the provisos to paragraphs 11 and 12(i) 
of the West Bengal Baby Food Licensing Order, 1966, 
it is hereby ordered— 

(i) that the period of validity of the existing Baby 
Food licences be extended up to the 30th 
day of April 1967 and 


(ii) that the date for filing applications for rene- 
wal of licences under the said order be ex- 
‘tended up to the 218 1 day of April 1967.

Jalpaiguri Division—Jalpaiguri 


No. {50P.W.—Ist April 1967—Whereas I, the 
Commissioner, Jalpaiguri Division, Jalpaiguri, West 
Bengal, deem the Kulkuli Shingser Channel ferry 
over the river Raidak 11 in the district of Jalpaiguri, 
declared as a public ferry by notification No. 38. 
P.W., dated the 14th August 1933, published at page 
1211 of Part I of the “Calcutta Gazette” of the 24th 
August 1933 (hereinafter referred to as the said public 
ferry) as unnecessary, a bridge having been  cons- 
tructed over the said river; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by clause (f) of section 6 of the Bengal Ferries Act, 
1885 (Bengal Act I of 1885), read with Government 
of West Bengal Notification No. [W(C), dated the 
12th June 1962, published at page 1816 of Part I of 
the “Calcutta Gazette,” dated the 5th July 1962, I, 
the Commissioner, Jalpaiguri Division, Jalpaiguri, 
West Bengal, hereby discontinue the said public ferry 
with effect from the date of issue of this notification.

The present reference uncor section 10 of the Indus- 
trial Disputes Act arises out of an industrial dispute 
between the Calcutta Silk Manufacturing Co. Ltd. 
(hereinafter cescribed as the Company), 23 B.T.Road, 
P.O. Sukchar, 24-Parganas and their workmen represent- 
ed by Calcutta Silk Manufacturing Workers’ Union, 
(hereinafter referred to as the Union), B.T. Road, P.O. 
Sukchar, 24-Parganas. The issue relates to the quan- 
tum of bonus to which the workmen mentioned in lists | 
and 2 attached to the order of reference are entitled to 
for the accounting years 1962-65, 1963-64 and 1964-65, 


The parties duly appeared and filed their written 
statements. Today the caso was fixed for hearing. On 
9181 March 1967 a joint petition of compromise settling 
the dispute was filed. On hearing the parties I am 
satisfied that the compron ise is voluntary, legal and 
proper. A copy of the memorandum of settlement 
has been filed along with the petition. As prayed for 
by the parties, I pass an award in terms of the said 
Memorandum of Settlement which shall form part 
hereof as Annexure “A’’.

agreed to settle the dixputes in respect of the above four 
financial years on the following terms and conditions.

1. It is agreed that the management will give at the 
rate of 2 1/2 day extra wages per year in settlement. of 
9 years bonus dispute (1962-63, 1963-64 and 1964-65) 
pending before the 4th Industrial Tribunal and 8 per 
cont. (i.e. 75 per cent.) of their annual carning for the 
bonus matter for the yoar 1965-66 as an exgratia pay-

list No. 1 of the order of reference) who are working- 
in the Mill from April 1962 till the year ending March 
1966 for all completed years of service as mentioned in 
para. 2 below. This is a consolidated agreement for all 
the four years. The division of this exgratia payment 
into four years has been done for convenience. 


2. Those who have joined the Mill later than 1962-63 
will get only for those particular years in which they 
have worked at: the rate 2-1/2 days wages for one com- 
pleted year of service as follows plus their due advances

It uppears that though the Institute runs a 
Workshop where some jobs are conducted in busi- 
nesa-like way, it is separate from the principal 
organisation which is a non-profit-making Society 
established for a specific purpose in furtherance of 
national development and social welfare. It may 
be noted that in the preamble of the Indian Statis- 
tical Act, 1959, the Institute has been declared as 
an Institute of national importance. The princi- 
pal object of the Institute is to carry on research 
work, and in this sense it is of the nature of en 
educational institute. The Union has produced 
a circular (Ext. 1) wherein it is stated that Elec- 
tronic Data Processing and Computation Unit 
(EDPCU) had been formed for the purpose of 
operating the IBM 1401 Electronic Data Process- 


_ Ing System and মাত equipment on business 


like lines. But paragraph 2 of this circular shows 
that the EDPCU will function as a separate direct 
enterprise of the Institute outside the Research 
and Training School. and' other existing divisions 
or projects. It is thus clear that Research Unita 

are not connected with the Workshop. ; 


From the appointment letter, Ext. A-l, it 
uppears that Sm. Uma Sen was appointed in the 
Haematological Research Unit of the Research and 
Training Institute of the Indian Statistical Insti- 
tute. She was subsequently transferred to the 
Family Planning Research Unit. So she was 
connected with the research work carried on by 
the said Unit. In the circumstances the dispute 
is not an ‘industrial dispute’ and, accordingly, the 
reference is not maintainable. 


However, conceding for the sake of argument 
the dispute is an industrial dispute and the refe- 
rence is good, I have already shown that on the

of this .Act the Central Government has control 
over the 11151016006 im some respects, but it cannot 
be, strictly speaking, said that the Institute 1s 
heing run under the authority of the Central Gov- 


ernment. So I cannot agree with learned 
Advocute. 
Now, coming to the last objection that the 


lustitute is not an ‘industry’, both sides relied on 
the case of Delhi University as reported in 1963 
(11) L.L.d. 3385 (Supreme Court) where it has, 
been held that the work of ‘imparting education 
carrie on by educational institutions is not an 
‘industry’ within the meaning of section 2(j) of 
the Act. Section 2(j) defines industry as an 
business, trade, undertaking, manufacture or call- 
ing of employers and includes any calling, service, 
employment, handicraft, or industrial occupation 
or avocation of workmen. 


From. the Memorundum of Association of the 
Institute (Ext. G), the principal objecta of the 
Institute appear to be as follows: ‘‘ To promote 
the atudy and dissemination of knowledge of and 
research on statistics and other subjects relating 
to planning for national development and social 
welfare to provide for, and undertake, the collection 
of information, investigations, projects, and ope- 
rational research for purposes of planning and the 
improvement of the efficiency of management and 
production’’. : 


Of covrse, the Institute maintains a Develop- 
ment Workshop, and we get from 0.P.W. 1 Shri 
S. P. Bhattacharya, former Deputy Chief-in- 
charge of this Workshop that he joined the Insti- 
tute in 1945, an attempt was made to carry on 
Development activities regarding Desk Calculating 
machine, and the Workshop was engaged in diffe- 
rent maintenance activities for the calculating 
inachines which were being used by the Institute. 
In 1960 license was granted by the Central Cov- 
ernment for manufacture of Desk Culculating 
Machines Punched Card Equipments. At that 
time development activitics on those machines were 
carried on in large scale for the purpose of ulti- 
mately producing these 
establishment, viz., Messrs. Sankhya-Jantra (P) 
Ltd. According to Shri Bhattacharya, this was a 
different entity and not a part of this Institute. 
He further says that technical assistance by wa 
of producing components of the nature of hig 
precision was also rendered to some outside orga- 
nisations including the Defence Establishment, by

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LABOUR DEPARTMENT 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 1647-I.R./1R/1R-1/66.—18th April 1967.—The following draft of 
amendments which, in exercise of the power conferred by section 38 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Act 14 of ایس‎ the Governor proposes to 
make in the West Bengal Industria] Disputes Rules, 1958, as subsequently 
amended (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), is hereby published, as 
required by sub-section (1) of the said section for the information of persons 
likely to be affected thereby. 


The draft will be taken into consideration on or after the 26th June 1967 
and any objection or suggestion with respect thereto which may he receiv 
by the undersigned before that date will be duly considered. 


DRAFT AMENDMENTS 


l. ‘For rule 17, substitute the following rule, namely :— 


‘17. Summons by a Board or Court.—A summons issued by a Board 
of Conciliation or Court of Enquiry shall be in Form D-1 and 
may require any person to produce before it any books, papers or 
other documents and things in the possession of or under the 
control of such person in سد‎ way relating to the matter under 
investigation by the Board or Court which the Board or Court 
thinks necessary for the purposes of such investigation.”’ ; 


2. For rule 20, substitute the following rule, oamely :— 


‘20. Procedure at the first sitting.—At the first sitting of a Board of 
Conciliation or Court of Enquiry, the Chairman or the Presidi 
Officer, as the cuse may be, shall call upon the parties in s 
order دہ‎ he may think fit to state their case.’’;

3. After rule 20, insert the following rules, namely :— 


“20A. Notice to the parties.—Upon receipt of a reference from the 
Government under section 10, the Industrial Tribunal / Labour 
Court concerned shall issue notices in Form D-2 upon the parties 
to the dispute as mentioned in the order of reference, requiring 
them to appear before it on a specified date either by themselves 
or through their authorised representatives for necessary 
directions, ہے‎ 


20B. Statement of case or written statement.—(1) The Industrial 
Trrbunal /Labour Court shall on the date fixed in the summons 
for the appearance of the parties direct the party which appears 
to the Tribunal / Labour Court to be the party at whose instance 
the refergnce has been initiated or where no such purty can be 
ascertained, the patty, which, in the opinion of the Industrial 
Tribunal/Labour Court, ought to be required to state its case 
first (hereinafter referred to as the first party). to state its case, 
together with the grounds upon which the claim for relief is 
founded, in writing on a date fixed by the Industrial Tribunal / 
Labour Court which shall ordinarily be within two weeks from 
the date of the order. 


(2) After the first party hus complied with the order passed under sub- 
rule (1), the other party (hereinafter referred to as the second 
party) shall be usked to file its written statement on a date fixed. 

y the Industrial Tribunal/ Labour Court, which shall ordinarily" '

Act it is incumbent on the management to pay 
retrenchment compensation to the  retrenched 
workmen at the {ime of retrenchment, over and 
above one month's notice or one month’s notice 
pay in lieu of notice. In the instant case the 
Yompany did not pay or offer any such retrench- 
went compensation to any of the retrenched work- 
men at the time of retrenchment. The workmen 
were served with ×ص‎ notice, Ext. B, dated 19th March 
11000) wherein it was simply stated that they would

letter there was offer of one month’s pay in lieu

not as provided in section 261 of the Act. More- 
over there is no mention of retrenchment compensa- 
tion in this letter. \Shri Banerji says that the 
word ‘dues’ would include اس سر‎ conipensa- 
tion as well. But if we read the letter as a whole, 
it cannot be gathered that by the word ‘dues’ the 
workmen were offered retrenchment compensation 
as well. Of course, the management realised the 
mistake, and hy u subsequent letter, Ext. 1, dated 
3181 March 1966, ‘retrenchment compensation’ was 
specifically offered. But this was done 10 days 
after the retrenchment. Even in this letter one 
month’s pay in lieu of notice was offered as per

MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 


NOTIFICATIONS 


New Delhi, the lst October 1966 


G.S.R. 1530.—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of 
section 3 of the All India Services Act, 1151 (61 of 1951), the Central Gov- 
ernment, after consultation with the Governments of the States concerned, 
hereby makes the following rules further to amend the Indian Administra- 
tive Service (Recruitment) Rules, 1954, namely ہۓ‎ 


1. (1) These rules may be cnlled the Indian Administrative Service 
(Recruitment) Amendment Rules, 1966. 


(2) They shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the 
29th January, 1966. 


2 In the Indian Administrative Service (Recruitment) Rules, 1954,— 


(a) in sub-rule (1) of rule 4, after clause (a), the following clause shall 
be inserted, namely :-— 


‘‘(aa) by selection of persons from among released Emergency Com- 
missioned Officers and Short Service Commissioned Officers, 
commissioned in the Armed Forces of the Union after the )ہ1‎ 
November, 1962 ;” 


(9) after rule 7, the following rule shall be inserted, namely :— 


“JA. Recruitment by selection of persons from among released Emer- 
gency Commissioned Officers and Short Service Commissioned 
Officers commissioned in the Armed Forces of the Union after the 
first November, 1962. 


[Pass ۸ 


সপ) 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, MAY 11, 67 


2 a ee রোজার চা ہمز‎ en ہصح رہ ےس21‎ 


(1) Till the 28th day of January, 1971, 20 per cent. of the total number 
of vacancies to be filled on the results of the competitive examination referred 
to in clause (a) and selection referred to in clause (aa) of sub-rule (1) of 
rule 4 shall be reserved in favour of persons, being released Emergency 
Commissioned Officers and Short Service Commissioned Officers, commission- 
ed in the Armed Forces of the Union after the 1st November, 1962. 


2) The selection of persons referred to in sub-rule (1) for appointment 
to the Service against the vacancies reserved for them shall be made in 
accordance with such regulations as the Central Government may, from time 
to time, make in consultation with the Commission and the State 
Governments. 


(3) The regulations made under sub-rule (2) shall provide for the 
reservation in favour of candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes and 
the Scheduled Tribes to the extent not exceeding 124 per cent. and 5 per cent. 
respectively, of the number of vacancies to be filled on the results of each 
examination, 


(4) Candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes 
declared by the Commission to be suitable for appointment to the Service 
with due regard to the maintenance of efficiency of administration may be 
appointed to the vucaucies reserved for the candidates of the Scheduled Castes 
or the Scheduled Tribes, asx the case may be, under sub-rule (3). 


(0) 1 a sufficient number of persons referred to in sub-rule (1) of the 
requisite calibre 1s not available for filling the vacancies reserved for them, 
the unfilled vacancies shall be treated دہ‎ unreserved and filled on the results 
of the competitive examination referred to in clause (a) of sub-rule (1) of 
rule 4, but a corresponding number of vacancies shall be carried forward to 
the next succeeding yeur: 


Provided thut no vacancies shall be carried forward under this sub-rule 
for a period of more than four years. 


(6) The total number of vacancies reserved for the persons referred to 
in sub-rule (1) under this rule and for the members of the Scheduled Castes 
and Scheduled Tribes under any other rule or order for the time being in 


force in any yeur, shall not exceed 45 per cent. of the total number of 


vacancies to be filled in that year through the competitive examination and

THE INDIAN ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICE (EMERCENCY ۔058)‎ 
SIONED AND SHORT SERVICE COMMISSIONED OFFICERS) 


(APPOINTMENT BY COMPETITIVE EXAMINATION) RECULA- 
TIONS, 1966. 


G.8.R. 1532.—In pursuance of rule 7A of the Indian Administrative 
Service (Recruitment) Rules, 1954, the Central Government in consultation 
with the State Governments and the Union Public Service Commission, 
hereby makes the following regulations, namely :— 


1. Short title, commencement and duration.—(1) These regulations may 
be called the Indian Administrative Service (Emergency Commissioned and 
Short Service Commissioned Officers) (Appointment by Competitive Exami- 
nation) Regulations, 1966. 


(2) They shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the 
29th January, 1966. 


(8) They shall remain in force for a period of five years from the 29th 
January, 1966. 


2. Definition—In these regulations unless the context otherwise 
requires,— 


(a) ‘available vacancies’ means the vacuncies in the Service which, as 
determined by the Central Government under the provisions of 
sub-rule (2) of rule 4 of the recruitment rules, are to be filled 
by released Emergency Commissioned or Short Service Commis- 
sioned officers ; 


(b) ‘Commission’ means the Union Public Service Commission ; 


(c) ‘Examination’ means a competitive examination for selection of 
released Kmergency Commissioned or Short Service Commissioned 
Officers who were commissioned in the Armed Forces after 1st 
November, 1962, for the purpose of filling vacancies in the All 
India and Central Services (Class I and Class 11) reserved for 
them, held at such intervals as the Central Government may, in. 
consultation with the Commission, from time to time, determine ; 


(d) ‘list? means the list of candidates prepared under regulation 8; 


(e) ‘recruitment rules’ means the 10 Administrative Service 
(Recruitment) Rules, 154; 


(f) ‘Scheduled Castes’ and ‘Scheduled Tribes’ shall have the same 
meaning os are assigned to them in clauses (24) and (25) respec- 
tively of article 866 of the Constitution ; 


(g) ‘Service’ means the Indian Administrative Service; 


(h) all other words and expressions used in these regulations and not 
defined but defined in the recruitment rules shall have the mean- 
ings respectively assigned to them in those rules. 


3. Holding of Examination—(1) The examination shall be conducted 
by the Commission in the manner notified by the Central Government from 
ime to time. ۱ کا‎ | 


(2) The dates on which and the pluces at which the examination shall 
be held shall be fixed by the Commission. 


4, Conditions of eligibility.—In order to be eligible to compete at the 
examination, a candidate must satisfy the following conditions, namely :— 
(i) Nativnality.—(e) He must be a citizen of India; 
Or 


(b) He must belong to such categories of persons as may, from time to 
time, be notified in this behalf by the Central Government.

(21) Age.—He must not have attained the age of 24 years on the 181 
August of the year in which he joined the pre-Commission train- 
ing in the Armed Forces of the Union: 


Provided that the upper age linut may be reluxed in respect of such 
categories of persons as may, from time to time, be notified in 
this behalf by the Central Government, to the extent and subject 
to the conditions notified in respect of each such category. 


Gli) Educational Qualifications —He must have held, at the time of 
joining pre-Commission training in the Armed Forces of the 
Union, a degree of any University incorporated by an Act of the 
Central or State Legislature in India or other educational institu- 
tions established by an Act of Parliament or declared to be deem- 
ed as Universities under Section 3 of the University Grants Com- 
mission Act, 1956, or a foreign University approved by the Central 
Government from time to time, or possess a qualification which 
has been recognised by the Central Government for the purposes 
of admission to the examination: 


Provided that سب‎ 


(a) in exceptional cases, the Commission may treat as qualified a 
candidate who, though not possessing the qualifications pres- 
cribed in this clause, has passed examinations conducted by 
Other institutions of a standard which, in the opinion of the 
Commission, justifies the admission of the candidate to the 
examination; and 


(b) candidates who are otherwise qualified but have taken degrees 
from foreign Universities, which are not approved by the Cen- 
tral Government, may also be admitted to the examination at 
the discretion of the Commission. 


5. Attempts at the examination.—No cundidute shall be permitted to 
compete more than two times at the examination, the restriction being 
effective from the examination held in 1966: 


Provided that a candidate who had not attained the age specified in 
paragraph (ii) of regulation 4 on the Ist August of the year in which he 
joined the pre-Commuission training in the Armed Forces of the Union, but 
had attained that age on the Ist August of the year succeeding the year in 
which he joined the pre-Commission training, shall be permitted to compete 
only once at the examination. 


Note I.—A candidate shall be deemed -to have competed at the examinna- 
tion if he actually appears in any one or more subjects. 


Note II.—A candidate‘who is eligible to take only one chance must take 
the examination held in the year preceding the year of his release. 


Note III.—A candidate who is eligible to take two chances must take the 
examination held in the year preceding the year of his release and the year 
oi his release. 


6. Disqualification for admission to examination.—Any attempt on the 
part of the candidate to obtain support for his candidature by any means 
may be held by the Commission to disqualify him for admission to the 
examination. 


7. Commission's decision to be final.—The decision of the Commission 
as to the eligibility or otherwise of the candidate for admission to the 
examination shall be final and no candidate to whom a certificate of admis- 


gion hae not been issued by the Commission shall be admitted to the 


examination.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


LEGISLATIVE DEPARTMENT 


West Bengal Ordinance No. II of 1967 


THE CALCUTTA TRAMWAYS (AMENDMENT) 
ORDINANCE, 1967. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the Calcutta Tramways Ben. Act I 
Act, 1880 for the purpose and in the manner hereinafter °f 1880۰ 
appearing; 

AND WHEREAS both Houses of the Legislature of West 
Bengal are not in session and the Governor is satisfied that 
circumstances exist which render it necessary for her to take 
immediate action; | 


The Governor is pleased, in exercise of the power conferred 
by clause (1) of article 213 of the Constitution of India, to make 
and promulgatc the following Ordinance, namely:— 


Short title. 1. This Ordinance may be called the Calcutta Tramways 
(Amendment) Ordinance, 1967. 

Amend- 2. In section 9 of the Calcutta Tramways Act, 1880, for 

ment of 


section 9 of the words “shall have power from time to time to fix”, the words 
Ben. Act L“‘shall have power, with the previous consent of the State 
of 1880. * Government, to fix or revise” shall be substituted and 


shall be deemed to have been substituted with effect from the 
1st day of March, 1967. 


PADMAJA NAIDU,

PART VI.—Bills introduced in Parliament of India; Reports of Select Committees presented to Parliament 
and Bills published before introduction in Parliament 


LOK SABHA 
The following Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on the 
18th November, 1966 :— 
BILL No. 70 OF 1966 
A Bill further to amend the Indian Telegraph 406, 
5886 and the Indian Post Office Act, 1898. 


Be it enacted by Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of 
the Republic of India as follows :— 


1, (1) This Act may be called the Personal Liberties Short title 


(Restoration) Act, 1966. and com- ۱ 
(2) It shall come into force at once. 0007۰ 


2. Section 5 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, shall amena- 


be omitted. ment of 
Act 13 
of 1885, 
3. Section 26 of the Indian Post (00006 Act, 1898, shall Amend. 
be omitted. ment of 
Aot 6 of 
STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS 1898. 


Section 5 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, empowers 
the Central and State Governments to take possession of 
licensed telegraphs and to order interception of messages. 
Similarly, wnder section 26 of the Indian Post Office Act. 
1898, the Government is authorised to intercept postal 
articles for public good. ‘These sections were incorporated 
in the relevant Acts when India was under British rule and 
they have not so far been omitted. The present Bill seeks 
to omit these sections so as to safeguard the personal 
liberties of free citizens of India. 


New DELHI; YASHPAIL SINGH.

This matter has been taken up ona preliminary 
point. at tho instance of Messrs. Martin Burn 1400 and 
its 10 associated companies mentioned in the order of 
reference and has been heard with coneent of both 
the parties. Tho points taken were that the dispute 
mentioned in 19900 No. 1 is not a mattor specifiod im 
in tho Second and Third Schedule to tho Industrial 
Disputes Act, 1947, and ag euch tho order of referonce 
is invalid and without jurisdiction and eecondly their is 
no scope for raising an indurtrial dispute with 0 view 
to determine the basis of payment of bonus for the 
year 1903-64 under the Payment of Bonua Act in the 
instant cace. 


Facts leading to the present dispute may briefly be 
stated. On 27th Devembor 1965, Government of 
West Bengal, in the Labour Dopartment by order No. 
6887-1.R./IR/11L-23(D)/65, referred an _ industrial 
dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication on the issues 
mentioned above. On 4th of January 1966, Gov- 
emment of West Bongal, inthe Labour Department by 
Corrigendum No. 22-1.R./TR/11L-23(D)/65, corrected 
some portion of the order of reference which however 
is not very material for our purpose. By another 
order, dated 20th August 1966, Government of West 
Bengal, in the Labour Departnient No, 3330-1.R. /TR/ 
11L--23(D)/65, included another establishment in tho 
original order of reference as the establishment being of 
a similar nature was likely to be interested or affected 
by the said dispute. It followe therefore that as a 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, MAY 12, 7" 1467 


০ 
8 


7 end 


Ltd., and its associated companies. Section 10(4) 
of the Industrial Disputes Act lays down that the Tri- 
bunal is required to confine its adjudication to those 
polnts and matters incidental thereto, which have been 
specified by the approriate Government. The Suprome 
Court in the above cited case indicated the procodure 
to be followed in the proceeding which were pending 
before the Payment of Bonus Act came into forco, 
including those which were covered by section 33 of 
the footing that the provisions of 89061035893 and 34(2) 
of the Act did not affect the validity of the remaining | 
provisions of the Act and they could be completely 
separated. Having regard to the financial year of all 
the companies, it is clear that the claim for bonus 
relates to a financial year that is covered by tho provi- 
sions of section 33 of the Payment of Bonus Act and 
as such the Tribunal is not in a position to adjudicate 
Issue No. 2 on the basis of the existing reference. 
Tribunal accordingly decides that there is no basis of 
payment of bonus under the Payment of Bonus Act in 
the instant reference and Issue No. 2 must be answered 
accordingly. 


As reards Issue No. ] it is to be pointed out that 
this is not a matter specified either in Second or Third 


_ Schedule of the Act.It is true that the Third Schedule 


after providing for 10 items such as wages, compen- 
satory allowance, etc., provided for another item in 
the following words :— 


“any other matter that may be prescribed"’. 


But no such matter appears to have been prescribed 
and{there is nothing on record to show that any noti- 
fication to that effect was ever issued. Consequently 
it cannot be held that the dispute relates to Issue No. 1 
is a matter specified either within the Second or Third 
Schedule to the Act. Even assuming that an enquiry 
as to whether the head offices of all the associated 
companies were employees of Messrs. Martin Burn Ltd. 
is an industrial dispute, no useful purpose would be 
served by adjudicating the issue as the claim for bonus 
in the ‘second issue relating to all the associated 
companies were for a period covered by section 33 
of the Payment of Bonus Act which has been struck 
down by the Supreme Court and as such cannot be 
adjudicated by the Tribunal. That being the position 
the Tribunal must hold that tho roference so far as 
Issue No. |. is conceyned is incompetent and without 
jurisdiction. 


It follows therefore that the prvlimmary objections 
succeed and the reference is incompetent.

Now, if the claim of bonus relates to the financial 
year 1963-64, then it must have commenced on Ist of 
October 1968 and ended on 30th September 1964. If 
the employees at the head offices of the 10 associated 
companies are not accepted as employees of Martin 
Burn Ltd., then bonus payable to these employees 
must relate to the financial year of each company 
commencing on a day earlier than Ist of October 1963 
which is the date of commencement of the financial 
year of Martin Burn Ltd. 


It is conceded on behalf of the Union that if the 
employees are to be regarded as employees of Martin 
Burn Ltd., then in view of the Supreme Court decision 
in Jalan Trading Co. (P) Ltd., case reported in 1966 (IT) 
L.L.J., page 546, it was conceded that the payment of 
bonus could not be made. In the said case Supreme 
Court struck down the provision of section 33 of the 
Payment of Bonus Act as patently discriminatory. 
The Act was made applicable to factories and other 
establishments in respect of the accounting year com- 
mencing on any day in the year 1964 and every sub- 
sequent accounting year. The accounting year in 
relation to bonus was defined in section 2(i)(ii) of the 
Act as the period in respect of which any profit and loss 
account of the company laid before it in annual general 
meeitng is made up, whether that period is a year 
or not. By section 33, the Act was made applicable 
to pending industrial disputes (regarding payment of 
bonus relating to any accounting year not boing the 
accounting year earlier than the accounting year in 
any day in the year 1962, immediately before May 29, 
1965) before the appropriate Government or any 
Tribunal or other authority under the Industrial 
Disputes Act, 1947. 


As it has not been clearly shown that a dispute was 
pending immediately before the date on which the 
Payment of Bonus Act became operative, section 33 
would not be attracted in this case, but even assuming 
that the dispute relating to the instant case was then 
awaiting conciliation before the Conciliation Officer or 
awaiting decision of thé Government in the matter of 
reference, section 33 of the Act having been struck 
down, bonus in the instant case cannot be determined 
under the provisions of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965. 
The Supreme Court further held that provisionofsection 
34(2) was arbitrary and unreasonable and hence void. 
There is little doubt that the accounting year in respect 
of each company as claimed is an accounting year not 
earlier than the accounting year ending on any day in 
the year 1962 and not later than the accounting year 
commencing on any day in the year 1964. That being 
the position, section 33 of the Payment of Bonus Act 
would also he attracted if there was a pending dispute. 
Had section 33 not being struck down and a dispute 
was pending either beforethe Government or any other 
authorities under the Industrial Disputes Actor in other 
corresponding law, there would have been no difficulty. 
Inauch a case the Tribunal could very well adjudicate 
the issuo. As the relevant provisions of the Payment 
of Bonus Act undor which the present dispute can be 
said to the governed has been struck down, there is no 
oth r question | -ft fur consid-iration by th> Tribunal, It 
is well settled that the Tribunal! cannot go behind the 
terms of reference and it isnotopento the Tribunal 
to consider any other alternative in the matter of pay- 
ment of bonus to the workmen of Measrs. Martin Burn

ORDER 


No. 3338-F.8./FS/14R-87 /67.—16th May 1967.— 
In exercise of powers conferred by rection 3 of the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955), read 
with the Government of India, Ministry of Food, 
Agriculture, Community Development and Co-operation 
(Department of Food), Order No. G. 5. R. 906, dated 
the 9th June 1966, as subsequently amended, the 
Governor is pleased hereby to make, with the prior 
concurrence of the Central Government, the following 
amendment in the West Bengal Rice and Paddy (Noti- 
fication of Movoment) Order, 1967, issucd under this 
department Order No. 2859-F.8./FS /14R-87 /67, dated | 
the26thApril 1967, published in the ‘“‘Calcutta Gazette, 
Extraordinary’’, of the 26th April 1967 (hereinafter 
referredtoas thesaid Order), namely سے‎ 


Amendment 


In paragraph 2 of the said Order, for clause (f) and 
Explanation thereunder, substitute the following clause 
and Explanation, namely :— 


‘(f) “free limit’’ means, in the case of paddy, a 
quantity not exceeding 3.75 quintals or, in 
the case of rice, a quantity not exceeding 


1481 


1482 THE OAL. GAZ., EXTRY.,. MAY 16, 1967 {Part I 


SS وش شش‎ ae Gea EE এত 00 


2.62 quintals or, in the case of both paddy 
and rice in any combination, a quantity not 
excecding, in the aggregate, 3.75 quintals 
of paddy and paddy equivalent of rice taken 
together. 


Explanation.—Eor the purpose of this clause, the 
expression “‘paddy equivalent of rice’’ means 
in respect of a quantity of rice a quantity of 
paddy equal to one and a half times the quan- 
tity of rice’.

Transport 


NOTIFICATIONS 


No. 1855-WT.—27th February 1967.—In exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 71 of the Calcutta Hackney-Carriage Act, 1919 
(Bengal Act ۱ of 1919), the Governor is pleased hereby to make the following 
by-laws for the Kalyani Notified Area (hereinafter referred to as the said 
Notified Area) in the district of Nadia, namely:— 


By-laws 


1. Definitions.—In these by-laws, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,— 

(a) “The Act” means the Calcutta Hackney-Carriage Act, 1919 (Bengal 
Act 1 of 1919); ۱ 

(9) “Commissioncr” means a Commissioner of the Municipality. 

(c) “Rickshaw” means a cycle-rickshaw as defined in clause (8) of section 
4 of the Act. 

2. Appointment and duties of the Registering Officer.—Every rickshaw in 
the Kalyani Notified Area (hereinafter referred to as the said Notified Area) 
shall be annually registered on such date as the Commissioners may direct, by a 
Registering Officer specially appointed for the purpose by the State Government 
by a notification in the Official Gazette. The Registering Officer shall keep the 
registers in accordance with the provisions of the Act and shall enter therein the 
particulars specified in these by-laws. 

3. Qualifications and conditions for issue of bearer’s license.—-Every person 

"applying for a rickshaw bearer’s licence shall be required to satisfy the 
Registering Officer— 

(a) that he knows how to drive and control a rickshaw; 

(b) that he is well-acquainted with the principal streets, offices and places 
in and around the said Municipality. 

(c) that he has a thorough knowledge of the tables of fares and distances 
prepared by the Commissioners in this behalf; 

(d) that he knows that rules of the road and the conventional signals used 
by the bearers and drivers of vehicles and by the Traffic police; 

(c) that he is between 18 and 45 years of age on the date of the application 
for issue of the Rickshaw bearer’s liccnse; and 

(f) that he is both physically and in all other respects a fit person for such 
employment. ۱

4. Contents of license.—There shall be affixed to each license issued to the 
bearer of a rickshaw— 


(a) the thumb mark or the signature of the bearer; 


(০) -a 0م"‎ card size photograph of the bearer to be supplied by him:

(c) a printed table of fares and distances prepared by the Commissioners, 
for which no charge shall have to be paid by the bearer. 


5. Production of license, 6৫০৮৮765519 bearer of a rickshaw shall carry with 
him his license and shall produce it whenever called upon to do so by any 
policeman on duty, any Commissioner or any other person authorised by the 
Commissioncrs in this behalf. 


6. Condition of rickshaws.—<(1)} The body of the rickshaw shall be kept 
sound and clean and all the boards shall be strong and properly secured. 


(2) The wheels shall be fitted with pneumatic tyres, and shall be strong and 
sound so as to run smoothly, without rattling or shaking and shall be protected 
by properly fitted splash boards. 


(3) The springs and axles shall be of good metal, strong and properly 
rivetted and free from rust. 


(4) The iron support at the back which shall be of good metal, strong and 
free from rust shall be properly curved and securely fixed on each side. 


(5) The hood, apron and cushions shall be made of, and covered with, good 
cloth, canvas or other material approved of by the Commissioners at a meeting. 


(6) The shafts shall be of strong wood, securely fixed, furnished at the 
foreend with a ring-shaped metal support and connected by a collision guard. 


(7) The hood and apron shall be so fitted as to make the vehicle water-tight. 


(8) Every rickshaw shall have two good lamps—one facing the front and the 
other the rear. 


(9) The lamp facing the rear shall have a red glass-cover and shall be so 
placed that the light through the cover be visible from a point ten metres in the 
rear of the centre of the vehicle. 


(10) Each arm of the rickshaw shall be so constructed as to serve as a 
support to the passenger. 


(11) Every rickshaw shall have a bell or a horn, as may be approved of by 
the Commissioners, affixed to the handle bars or cross bars on the cycle in such 
a way that it can be operated by fingers and give continuous ringing as and when 
necessary. 


7. Dimensions and pattern of rickshaws.—Every rickshaw shall conform to 
the following dimensions and be of such pattern as may be specified by the 
Commissioners at a mecting:—

10. Speed and halting charges of rickshaws.—When a rickshaw is hired, the 
bearer shall ordinarily drive . the same at a speed of not 1635 than thirteen 


kilometres per hour. If a rickshaw after being hired is made to halt, halting 
charge shall be paid according to the scale laid down in the fare table in by-law 


11. Passengers are to pay other charges.—Passcngers are to pay the ferry 
and other similar charges over and above the ratcs payable to the bearers of 
rickshaw. 


12. Prohibition of smoking, etc——While driving, the bearer of a rickshaw 
shall not smoke or muffle up his face in such a manner as to endanger the 
proper driving of his vehicle. 


13. Maximum load to be carried in_ rickshaw.—The total weight of the 
passengers and the luggage, if any, carried in a rickshaw shall not exceed 150 


kilograms. 


14. Advertisement on rickshaws.—No advertisement shall be displayed on 
the body of a rickshaw without the previous permission of the Commissioners 
and when such permission is obtained, it shall be displayed in such a manner as 
not to cover either wholly or partly the number plate and the fare table affixed 
to the rickshaw. 


15. Rickshaws to wait at stand.—Every rickshaw while at rest, shall be 
parked at a stand fixed by the Commissioners for such purpose.

16, Power of entry.—It shall be lawful for a Commissioner or any other 
person authorised in this behalf by the Chairman or the Commissioners, at any 
time between sun-risc and sun-set, to cnter any premises in which any licensed 
rickshaw or any other thing used ‘therewith are kept, in order to carry out any 
of the provisions of the Act or of these by-laws, and the owner or occupier of 
the premises or his agent, as the case may be, shall afford every reasonable 
facility to such Commissioner or person for such inspection. 


17. Tables of fares and distance.—The Commissioners shall cause to be 
prepared and kept printed copies of the table of fares and distances for sale to 
the public at a price fixed by the Commissioners, 


18. Refusal to ply.—No bearer of a rickshaw shall, except on reasonable 
grounds, refuse to ply the rickshaw on hire. 


19. Particulars of registers.—The registers and licenses maintained and 
issued under the Act shall contain the following particulars, namely:— 


(A) Bearer’s license 


(1) Number of the license. 

(2) Name, father’s name, place of abode, present address and age of the 
person to whom the license is granted. 

(3) Date on which the license is granted. 

(4) Number of the rickshaw allowed to the bearer. 

(5) Photograph of the bearer. 

(6) Date of expiry of license. 

(7) A summary of the: more important statutory provisions and by-laws 
affecting bearers of rickshaws. 

(8) Signature of the Registering Officer. 


(B) Owner’s license 


(1) Number assigned to the rickshaw in the register. 

(2) Name, father’s name and place of residence of the owner, the 
description of the rickshaw and the place Where the rickshaw is 
kept. 

(3) Number of passengers the rickshaw is licensed to carry. 

(4) Date on which the license is granted. 

(5) Date of expiry e@f the license. 

(6) Signature of the Registering Officer. 


(C) Register of rickshaws 


(1) Number Assigned to the rickshaw in the register. 
(2) Fee réceipt number. 

(3) Date on which the license is granted. 

(4) Name and father’s name of the owner. 

(5) Owner’s place of residence. 

(6) Place where the rickshaw is kept. 

(7) House number 

(8) Name and father’s name of the bearer. * 

(9) Bearer’s place of residence. 

(10) Period of suspension, if any. 

(11) Date of renewal. 

(12) Particulars of duplicate ticket, if any. 

(13) Particulars of duplicate license, if any. 
(14) Photograph of the bearer. 
(15) Date of conviction, if any. 
(16) Section of Jaw under which convicted. 
(17) Punishment inflicted. 

(18) Date of offence. 

(19) Particulars constituting the offence. 

(20) In case of transfer of ownership of the rickshaw, the name of the 

transferee. 

(21) Date of transfer. 

(22) Number of person the rickshaw is licensed to carry. 
(23) Signature of the Registering Officer. 
(24) Remarks.

COVERNMENT OF WEST BENCAL 


LABOUR DEPARTMENT 


BEFORE THE FOURTH INDUSTRIAL 
TRIBUNAL, WEST BENGAL. 


Present: 


Shri R. BHATTACHARYA, Judge. 
Appearance : 


For the Union—Shri N. 1), Shrimani, Advocate. 
For the Company—Shri Satish Sen, Advocate. 


AWARD 


This is a reference under section 10 of the Indus- 
trial Disputes Act. The parties are Messrs. Electro 
Steel Casting Limited (hereinafter described as the 
Company), P.O. Sukchar, 24-Parganas, with Head 
Office at No. 4, Dalhousie Square East, Calcutta-1 
and their workmen represented by Dalmia Iron and 
Steel Mazdoor Union, Nutan Bazar, Khardah, 
24-Vargaunas (hereinafter described as the Union). 
The issue for determination is as follows: 


Issud 


Whether the termination of service of Shri 
Pannalal Shaw is justified? What relief, if 
any, is he entitled toP 


In short the case of the Union in its written state- 
ment 18 that Shri Pannalal Shaw was appointed a 
fitter on 196 March 1964 against a permanent vacan- 
cy in the Company. During the tenure of his 
service he maintained a good and spotless record. 
He was an active member of the Union. It has 
been alleged that at times he was very much over- 
burdened with excessive overtime work and as a 
result thereof, his health was affected. He had to 
express his inability to do any further overtime 
work. This, according to the 72 incurred the 
displeasure of the Company. By a letter, dated

Whereas under the Government of West Bengal, 
Labour Department, order No. 2086-I.R. /IR/10L- 
76/66, dated the 26th May 1966, the industrial dis- 
pute between Messrs. Electro Steel Castings 
Limited, P.O. Sukchar, 24-Parganas era Office 
at No. 4, Dalhousie Square East, Calcutta), and 
their workmen represented by Dalmia Iron and Steel 
Mazdoor Union, Nutun Bazar,  Khardah, 
24-Parganas, regarding the issue mentioned in the 
said order being a matter specified in the second 
schedule to the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (XIV 
of 1947), was referred for adjudication to the 
Fourth Industrial Tribunal ; 


And whereas the said Fourth Industrial. Tribunal 
has submitted to the State Government its award 
on the said industrial dispute ; 


Now, therefore, is pursuance of the provisions of 
section 17 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 
(XIV of 1947), the Governor is pleased hereby to 
تر‎ the said award as shown in the annexure 
1ereto. 


ANNEXURE 


In the matter of an industrial dispute between 
Messrs. Electro Steel Casting Limited, P.O. 
Sukchar, 24-Parganas (Head Office at No. 4, 


Dalhousie Square East, Calcutta-1), and their . 


workmen represented by Dalmia Iron and Steel 
Mazdoor Union, Nutan Bazar, Khardah, 
24-Parganas, referred under C. 0. No. 2085- 
1.R./1R/10L-76/66, dated 26th May 1966. 
(Case No. ۷۱۱۱۲ ۰۱۴9/66.( 


[Part IC
